items.stem: A horizontal beam is pinned at one end and supported by a cable at the other. To find the cable tension, what should you do first?

options.text: Draw a free-body diagram and sum moments about the pin
options.rationale: Correct: taking moments about the pin removes the unknown pin reaction and isolates the cable tension.
Temperature is irrelevant to a static force balance here.

options.text: Assume the tension equals the beam's weight
options.rationale: Tension depends on geometry and load position, not simply the weight.

options.text: Sum forces only in the horizontal direction
options.rationale: Horizontal equilibrium alone cannot solve a vertical load problem.

items.explanation: Correct: taking moments about the pin removes the unknown pin reaction and isolates the cable tension.

items.stem: Which TWO quantities must you know to compute the factor of safety of a ductile part in tension? (Select TWO.)

options.rationale: Correct: for a ductile part the yield strength sets the allowable stress.

options.text: The applied (working) stress in the part
options.rationale: Correct: factor of safety is the yield strength divided by the working stress.
Colour has no bearing on mechanical strength.
Humidity does not define the static factor of safety in this basic case.

items.explanation: Correct: for a ductile part the yield strength sets the allowable stress.

items.stem: A reducing gear train increases torque at the output. What necessarily happens to the output rotational speed?

options.text: It decreases in proportion to the gear ratio
options.rationale: Correct: in an ideal gear train speed drops as torque rises, conserving power.
Speed and torque trade off inversely in a gear reduction.

options.text: It stays the same as the input
options.rationale: A reduction changes the speed; only a 1:1 ratio keeps it equal.
The output still turns; it is only slower.

items.explanation: Correct: in an ideal gear train speed drops as torque rises, conserving power.
